neighbours.label: placing a device or probe in contact with a body or surface (on the chest, against the skin, implanted in)
fire: Tape the electrode on the patient's left wrist before the scan.
The nurse pressed the stethoscope against the baby's back.
A tiny chip was implanted under the dog's skin.
Attach the thermometer probe to the side of the tank.
The doctor placed the ultrasound wand on her belly.
A catheter is threaded into the artery through the groin.
Clip the pulse oximeter onto your index finger.
The technician fixed the sensor patch against his chest.
quiet: The electrode report was sent to the patient's doctor.
The nurse cleaned the stethoscope after the baby's checkup.
A tiny chip stores the dog's owner details.
The thermometer probe beeps when the water is ready.
The doctor ordered a new ultrasound wand for the clinic.
A catheter costs less than the older surgical option.
The pulse oximeter shows a number on its screen.
The technician walked into the lab with his coffee.

predictions: Fires on the placement word (on/against/into/implanted) when a sensor, probe or electrode is put on a body or object; quiet on the same devices doing something else and on people moving into places.
notes: Probe: 'sensor on the patient's chest' 0.30, 'held gently against your pet's skin' 0.20, 'implanted in the brain' 0.18, 'inserted ... into the heart' 0.10; 'probe sends data' 0.02, 'walked into the room' 0.01. Peaks are modest.
